name: Naegeli-Franceschetti-Jadassohn Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Naegeli-Franceschetti-Jadassohn Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of reticulate (net-like) hyperpigmentation primarily on the trunk and neck
Congenital absence or marked reduction of dermatoglyphics (fingerprints and palm prints)
Dental abnormalities including hypodontia, enamel hypoplasia, and early tooth loss
Hypohidrosis or anhidrosis leading to heat intolerance
Nail abnormalities such as dystrophic or hypoplastic nails

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: reticulate hyperpigmentation, absent dermatoglyphics, and dental anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in the KRT14 gene can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dental anomalies including hypodontia and enamel hypoplasia

common.symptomName: Hypohidrosis or anhidrosis (reduced or absent sweating)
Mild hair abnormalities including sparse scalp hair

occasional.symptomName: Heat intolerance with episodes of hyperthermia
Hypoplasia of sweat glands on histology

rare.symptomName: Mild palmoplantar hyperhidrosis in some cases
Rare nail infections secondary to dystrophy

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal changes with pigment incontinence
other: Absence of dermatoglyphics on fingerprint analysis
Dental radiographs showing hypodontia and enamel defects

distinguishingFeatures: Reticulate hyperpigmentation primarily in flexural areas

redFlags: Severe hypohidrosis leading to recurrent hyperthermia
Early tooth loss causing feeding difficulties
Marked absence of dermatoglyphics complicating forensic identification
references: Orphanet Report on Naegeli-Franceschetti-Jadassohn Syndrome, Orphanet 237
Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
